_meta.description: Physical validation rules for mammals and birds commonly photographed in everyday scenes. Self-describing: each rule carries its own predicate, parameters, and severity. No interpreter vocabulary file is required.
_meta.generated_by: handcrafted; mirrors the structure the generic LLM rule-generation prompt would produce

subtype_notes.chicken: Chickens are bipedal (2 legs), have 2 wings, and a beak. Wings attach laterally or mid-dorsally to the torso.
subtype_notes.dog: Dogs are quadrupedal (4 legs), no wings, no beak. Tail length varies by breed.
subtype_notes.cat: Cats are quadrupedal (4 legs), no wings, no beak. Tail typically long and flexible.
subtype_notes.horse: Horses are quadrupedal (4 legs), no wings, no beak. Tail of hair hanging from posterior.
subtype_notes.sheep: Sheep are quadrupedal (4 legs), no wings, no beak. Short tail, often barely visible.
subtype_notes.cow: Cows are quadrupedal (4 legs), no wings, no beak. Tail hangs from posterior.
subtype_notes.squirrel: Squirrels are quadrupedal (4 legs), no wings, no beak. Bushy tail typically same length as body.
subtype_notes.elephant: Elephants are quadrupedal (4 legs), no wings, no beak. Head includes trunk extension; legs are heavy and columnar.
subtype_notes.generic_animal: Unknown animal type. Apply only universal physical constraints.

rules.description: No anatomical features outside the species' canonical part inventory.
Every animal must have at least a torso and a head visible.
An animal has exactly one torso.
An animal has exactly one head.
Leg count depends on species: birds are bipedal, mammals are quadrupedal.
One eye visible in profile view, two in frontal view.
Tail may be occluded or minimal in some views.
Wings are valid only for birds.
Beak is valid only for birds.
Chickens have up to two wings (may be occluded/closed)
Chickens have one beak.
Eyes must lie within the head region.
Beak must lie within the head region.

Legs must not be on the head. Uses a bilateral overlap test: a leg's bbox falling inside a much-larger head bbox does not fire unless the intersection also occupies a meaningful fraction of the head's area. This prevents false positives when the head bbox is inflated by attached anatomy (e.g. a hanging trunk, snout, or mane) that extends down past the body.
Wings must not overlap the head.
Beak must be on the head, not the torso.
Tail must not overlap an eye.
Legs must be attached to the torso.
Head is at one of the anterior ends of the body along the image x axis (either leftmost or rightmost depending on which way the animal faces).
Tail is on the opposite end of the body from the head.
Legs attach below the torso centroid.
Beak projects forward from the head.

Head width is a sensible fraction of torso width. Bounds vary by species: elephants/cows/horses/sheep use relaxed bounds because (a) those species have proportionally large heads and (b) their torso bbox is often foreshortened in non-lateral views, inflating the ratio.
Leg height is 30-150% of torso height. Wider bounds tolerate non-lateral views where the torso bbox is vertically compressed by foreshortening.
Tail length is 10-80% of torso length.
Wing spread is 50-150% of torso length.
Eye diameter is 5-15% of head width.
Beak length is 20-40% of head length.

Head area should not vastly exceed torso area (tolerance allows up to 2x torso area, to accommodate close-ups, non-lateral views, and species where the head bbox includes attached anatomy like trunks).
Eye is smaller than head.
If an eye is detected, a head must also be detected.
If a leg is detected, a torso must also be detected.

llm_prompt_template:
You are a zoology and animal anatomy expert assessing whether a detected set of components plausibly describes a real animal of the stated species.

SPECIES: {subtype} (id: {subtype_id})
CAPTION: "{caption}"
{subtype_notes}
DETECTED COMPONENT COUNTS:
{counts_json}

DETECTED BOUNDING BOXES (pixel coordinates, center-format):
{boxes_json}

Detection confidence (image-level aggregate): {ensemble_confidence}

RULES BEING CHECKED BY THE PHYSICAL VALIDATOR (for your reference):
{rule_summary}

=== YOUR TASK ===

Assess whether the detected configuration is physically plausible for a real {subtype}.
Be tolerant of detection noise (e.g., one fewer leg visible due to occlusion).
Do NOT penalize purely because some bounding boxes are missing.

Consider:
1. COMPONENT COUNTS: Do the detected counts match typical {subtype} anatomy?
2. SPATIAL RELATIONSHIPS: Are head/torso/limbs/tail in anatomically correct positions?
3. SPECIES-SPECIFIC FEATURES: Are features like beak/wings present only on birds, absent on mammals?
4. OBVIOUS IMPOSSIBILITIES: Floating parts, impossible orientations, etc.
5. ANATOMICAL INCONSISTENCIES: List any anatomical features visible in the image that are inconsistent with the species named in the caption.
6. NON-BIOLOGICAL/HUMAN-LIKE FEATURES: List any features that appear non-biological or human-like.

=== RESPOND IN EXACTLY THIS FORMAT ===

SCORE: [0-100 integer or decimal]
VERDICT: [PASS if >=60, FAIL if <60]
SUBTYPE: {subtype}
CONFIDENCE: [0.0-1.0]
SPECIFICATION_VIOLATIONS: [bullet list of count/type mismatches, or None]
SPATIAL_VIOLATIONS: [bullet list of impossible placements, or None]
REASONING: [3-5 sentences summarizing your assessment]
